how: Each entry below was written after opening the saved picture, thread or linked reading. Where an axis was unreadable the number is left out rather than guessed. A bookmark with no entry here was captured but not yet looked at.

2080404535177265191.shows: A one-glance verdict card: the words GLOBAL LIQUIDITY at the top, a single large word for the state - UNSUPPORTIVE - a small forecast sparkline from today, then three labelled rows: Regime HEDGE, Weekly change +2.785, Daily status decreasing. The thread behind it runs the same way: a plain sentence, then the levels.
2080404535177265191.method: One measure, one verdict word, one small picture, three rows. The judgement is made for you before any chart is read.
2080404535177265191.data_needed: Any measure the Hub already computes, plus a rule that turns it into one word.
2080404535177265191.hub_has: Yes - Geiger, breadth and the rails all produce numbers today; none of them says a word.
2080404535177265191.build: Small: a card component plus one wording rule per measure.
2080404535177265191.recommendation: Build this first. It is the shape Alan liked in the feed, and it fits every reading the Hub already has.
2080404535177265191.why: It is the fast statement Alan asked for, it costs no new data, and every existing Hub measure can wear it.

2082071069859737812.shows: Two pieces. First a report table, How Long Until Tech Recovers - every technology drawdown since 1998: event, drawdown, bottom date, days to bottom, days to a new high, and whether it recovered. Median of nine recoveries: -25.7%, 73 days to the bottom, 108 days to a new high, nine of nine recovered. The current episode is its own row, -12.0%, 56 days, days-to-high Pending. Second a chart, 2026 versus the most similar years: S&P 500 year-to-date return by trading day with 1968, 1978 and 2007 drawn behind 2026 and a dashed projected path.
2082071069859737812.method: Find every past episode of the same kind, measure how deep and how long each one took, then put today's unfinished episode in the same table as a pending row.
2082071069859737812.data_needed: Long daily history for the index or sector, and a rule for what starts and ends an episode.
2082071069859737812.hub_has: Partly - the chart API holds daily bars for the 364-symbol universe; how far back it goes for an index proxy needs checking before promising 1998.
2082071069859737812.build: Medium: the episode finder is small, the honest history check is the work.
2082071069859737812.recommendation: Build the table for whatever history we actually hold, and show the current episode as pending. Leave the projected path out - it is a claim, not a measurement.
2082071069859737812.why: It answers the question Alan keeps asking - how long does this take to play out - with counted history instead of an opinion.

2089405550102528044.shows: No picture: a short post saying what each timeframe implies about timing. Four-hour chart, expect a move in 4 to 10 days. Daily chart, 8 to 20 days. Weekly chart, 2 to 5 months. The ten-post thread works through examples.
2089405550102528044.method: Attach an expected waiting time to the timeframe a signal came from, so a signal is never read as immediate.
2089405550102528044.data_needed: Nothing new - only the rung a reading came from.
2089405550102528044.hub_has: Yes. The Equalizer rungs are exactly these timeframes.
2089405550102528044.build: Small: one line of wording per rung.
2089405550102528044.recommendation: Put the expected horizon beside every Geiger rung. It turns a colour into a plan without changing a single calculation.
2089405550102528044.why: It is free, it uses Alan's saved rungs untouched, and it stops a 2-hour reading being mistaken for a two-day one.

2082445628332753174.shows: A weekly chart of the percentage of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day average, 2023 to 2026, on a 0-100 scale. A straight line drawn across the rally peaks slopes downward: each rally since 2024 has topped out on fewer participants than the one before. The latest bar, 71.57, pokes just above that line.
2082445628332753174.method: Count participation instead of price, then draw the peaks to show whether rallies are getting broader or thinner.
2082445628332753174.data_needed: Daily closes and a 50-day average for every index member.
2082445628332753174.hub_has: Yes - the Hub stores daily bars for all 364 symbols; this is a count, not a new source.
2082445628332753174.recommendation: Build it as a weekly line with the peak trendline, and show today's value as a number beside it.
2082445628332753174.why: The cheapest honest measure of whether a rally is real, from data already on disk.

2064000748543975599.shows: Daily combined share volume of the 3x leveraged ETFs - SPXL, SPXS, SOXL and SOXS - from June 2016 to August 2026. It sits under 100 million for years, steps up through 2022, and then spikes to about 1.1 billion shares in the last bar, circled as a record. Source marked Goldman Sachs.
2064000748543975599.method: Use the volume of the most speculative instruments as a froth gauge, on a long enough history that a record is visible as a record.
2064000748543975599.data_needed: Daily share volume for four ETF tickers.
2064000748543975599.hub_has: Needs checking - these four tickers are not necessarily in the 364-symbol universe, but they are ordinary listed ETFs the chart API can carry.
2064000748543975599.build: Small, once the tickers are in the universe.
2064000748543975599.recommendation: Build it. Alan approved this one by name, and it is four symbols and a sum.
2064000748543975599.why: Alan asked for it, it is tiny, and it measures crowd behaviour nothing else on the Hub measures.

2066204017274048727.shows: A dark NVDA daily chart with a single blue line labelled 2026 lows aVWAP - volume-weighted average price anchored to this year's low - rising from about 168 to about 205. Price is sitting exactly on it at 205.42 with the note Decision time. A volume-by-price profile runs down the right edge showing where the shares actually changed hands.
2066204017274048727.method: Anchor a volume-weighted average to an event that mattered, then watch whether price holds it.
2066204017274048727.data_needed: Daily bars with volume, and a chosen anchor date.
2066204017274048727.build: Small for the line; medium if the volume-by-price profile comes too.
2066204017274048727.recommendation: Build anchored VWAP with three ready anchors - 52-week low, 52-week high and last earnings - and say which anchor is in use.
2066204017274048727.why: Alan approved it, the data is already here, and it gives a level with a reason instead of a round number.

2073287229754273939.shows: A rotation tool built in fifteen minutes. Four labelled buckets: LEADING strong and still rising, TURNING DOWN strong but rolling over, TURNING UP weak but catching up, LAGGING weak and falling, each holding sector chips. Below, a ranked ladder: rotation score, strength percent, momentum, and the change in four-week rank with an arrow. A Map / Ladder toggle at the top. The linked reading is the StockCharts explanation of relative rotation graphs.
2073287229754273939.method: Score every sector on strength against a benchmark and on the direction of that strength, then bucket it into four states and rank it.
2073287229754273939.data_needed: Daily closes for the sectors and one benchmark.
2073287229754273939.recommendation: Build the ladder first - it reads well on a phone - and keep the four-week rank change, which is the part that shows a turn early.
2073287229754273939.why: It turns a wall of sector lines into four buckets and a list, which is what Alan actually wants to see at a glance.

2077780068911489117.shows: An S&P 500 daily chart with RSI(14) on top, the 50-day average through the middle, two converging lines marked we are at the apex of this particular two lines, and, along the bottom, Bollinger Band Width at its lowest reading since before the April move, annotated Bollinger Bands getting oh so tight here.
2077780068911489117.method: Measure how narrow the bands have become relative to their own history; a squeeze precedes an expansion, direction unknown.
2077780068911489117.recommendation: Add band width as a percentile of its own last two years, and flag the lowest decile. Say plainly that it predicts size, not direction.
2077780068911489117.why: One line of arithmetic on data we hold, and it is the only Hub reading that would warn that a quiet tape is about to stop being quiet.

2066551882537951628.shows: Revenue plus price for Palantir: quarterly revenue as black bars climbing from about 0.2 billion in Q1 2019 to about 1.6 billion in Q1 2026, with the share price drawn over it as a blue line on its own axis. The point of the post - seven fast-growing companies in a drawdown - is the gap between a revenue line that keeps climbing and a price that has stalled.
2066551882537951628.method: Put the fundamental series and the price on one picture so a drawdown can be read against the business, not against sentiment.
2066551882537951628.recommendation: Put this on the company tile. It is the clearest single picture for deciding whether a fall is a discount or a downgrade.
2066551882537951628.why: Two series we already hold, one picture, and it answers the question Alan asks about every position.

2082500448733265969.shows: A SPY daily chart with one enormous downward wick hanging alone beneath the body of every nearby candle, down to roughly 717 while the surrounding bodies sit near 735-740. The post explains it printed in under a minute at 3:59 PM on Friday 26 June, and quotes the old desk saying: if it prints there, it will trade there.
2082500448733265969.method: Find prices that printed once and were never revisited, and keep them on the chart as unfinished business.
2082500448733265969.data_needed: Daily and intraday bars - the wick, and a check of whether price has since traded through it.
2082500448733265969.build: Small: flag a wick far longer than the recent average range, then mark the level until it is traded through.
2082500448733265969.recommendation: Build it as a level finder. It is cheap and nothing else on the Hub produces these levels.
2082500448733265969.why: A genuinely different kind of level, found automatically from bars we already store.

2079213251372646426.shows: A Goldman prime-book chart: trailing eight-week net flow in US information technology as a percentage of the sector's gross market value, 2017 to 2026, plotted as bars either side of zero. The final reading sits near -9.7%, below every other bar in the ten-year sample, marked with a red line and circle.
2079213251372646426.method: Take one flow measure, express it against its own ten-year history, and mark today's reading against that history.
2079213251372646426.data_needed: Prime brokerage flow, which is Goldman's own book.
2079213251372646426.hub_has: No, and it cannot be bought.
2079213251372646426.recommendation: Steal the presentation, not the data: any Hub measure shown as today's reading against ten years of the same measure. The prime-book number itself stays a screenshot.

2077838537521508804.shows: An Unusual Whales panel: intraday SPY price with aggregated net option premiums for every ticker in the index, net call premium and net put premium as separate lines, and net volume filled underneath. The end of the day is circled where the lines roll over together.
2077838537521508804.method: Add up option premium across the index constituents through the day and watch it against price.
2077838537521508804.build: Not buildable without buying an options feed.
2077838537521508804.recommendation: Leave it. Note it as the one idea in the folder that needs a data purchase, so the decision is Alan's and not silently dropped.

2081180171181113757.shows: Global stock market capitalisation as a percentage of global GDP, 2004 to 2026, at 136.9. The 2021 peak and the present reading are both circled; the line is at the top of its twenty-year range and above the 2007 high.
2081180171181113757.method: One slow valuation ratio against its own long history - a temperature, not a timing tool.
2081180171181113757.data_needed: Global market cap and global GDP, both macro series.
2081180171181113757.hub_has: No, but the macro job already pulls FRED-style series, so this is a new series rather than a new pipeline.
2081180171181113757.recommendation: Add it to the macro rail as a slow-moving temperature with its date stamp visible. It should never drive a trade signal.

2080303391826129327.shows: A five-minute S&P 500 chart after a gap down: the 20, 50 and 200 averages all sloping down, and price chopping sideways in a narrow band under the falling 20, labelled premium burning pattern with a large arrow.
2080303391826129327.method: Name the regime where price stops trending and simply bleeds option premium: narrow realised range while price stays under a falling short average.
2080303391826129327.hub_has: Yes - the chart API serves intraday intervals.
2080303391826129327.recommendation: Worth a small flag on the intraday view - chop, not trend - so a quiet tape is not read as a setup.

2070929757492117704.shows: Not a chart: a six-page research note, Loop Engineering for Self-Improving Hedge Funds - a framework for recursive agentic systems that generate alpha 24/7, plus a linked X article, How to use loop engineering to build a self-improving quant trading system. The capture holds the note's first three pages of text and the whole article; the argument is that one operator with agent loops covers the roles a desk staffs with data engineers, researchers, execution traders and risk officers.
2070929757492117704.method: A build pattern for the machinery around a strategy, not a market measure: maker, checker, execution and risk as separate agents inside one loop.
2070929757492117704.data_needed: None - it is about how the system is assembled.
2070929757492117704.recommendation: Worth Alan reading for how the Scintilla jobs are arranged, especially the maker-checker split. It is a practitioner essay, not evidence, and it promises alpha 24/7 - treat that claim with the suspicion it deserves.

2079224490081353763.shows: A one-page company sheet for ASML: financials, key metrics and valuation laid out on a single image, with the quarter's beats listed in the quoted post - EPS 7.59 against 6.88 expected, revenue 9.33 billion against 8.87 expected, gross margin 54.0% against 51.9%. The linked page is the full write-up.
2079224490081353763.method: One page per company: the few numbers that matter, the same layout every time, so companies can be compared at a glance.
2079224490081353763.data_needed: Fundamentals the Hub already stores, plus consensus estimates for the beat-or-miss columns.
2079224490081353763.hub_has: Partly - actuals yes, estimates are the gap.
2079224490081353763.recommendation: Use the layout for the Hub's own company tile, and show a beat only where an estimate is actually stored; otherwise show the actual alone.

2088364109838319907.shows: The picture is a portrait of the manager, not data - there is no chart in it. The holdings are in the post text: a 13F filing listing the fund's positions and share counts as of the end of the quarter.
2088364109838319907.method: Read quarterly regulatory filings to see what a named fund held.
2088364109838319907.build: Medium, and the data is 45 days stale by the time it is public.
2088364109838319907.recommendation: Low priority. If it is ever built, the staleness has to be printed beside every holding.
